newsitem.title: USA: Accused Unabomber makes TV appearance in N.J. court.
newsitem.headline: Accused Unabomber makes TV appearance in N.J. court.

text.p: Accused Unabomber Theodore Kaczynski appeared via closed circuit television in a New Jersey courtroom on Tuesday to plead not guilty to charges of mailing a deadly package bomb to a local advertising executive.

The judge in the case opted to reserve decision on whether to try Kaczynski on murder charges in New Jersey in addition to his scheduled trial next fall in California, where he faces charges in a terrifying 17-year bombing spree that killed three people and injured 23 others.

In an unusual video teleconference appearance from a jail in Sacramento, California, where he is being held without bail, the accused bomber appeared calm. He wore a closely cropped beard, a white shirt and a brown jacket without a tie. At times he put on a pair of reading glasses.
Kaczynski, who allegedly targeted universities and airlines in his deadly bombing campaign, answered "Yes, I do" in an emotionless voice as the judge asked if he waived his right to a Newark trial.
Prosecutors want to try Kaczynski in New Jersey in June, six months before his California trial begins on Nov. 12.
Kaczynski faces murder charges here in the Dec. 10, 1994 death of advertising executive Thomas Mosser, who was killed by a parcel bomb mailed to his home in North Caldwell, N.J.
The package exploded in Mosser's hands as he stood in his kitchen preparing to go Christmas tree shopping with his family.
Authorities claim Kaczynski mailed the bomb from San Francisco.
"With a capital murder, it is imperative that the case be held in New Jersey," said prosecutor Robert Cleary. "Justice must be served in the community where the act occurred.
Kaczynski's defence attorneys want the charges consolidated into one case in California, where Kaczynski is accused of four bomb attacks that killed two people and injured two others.
"The question is why do we need two trials?" his public defender Chester Keller said. "It's a waste of time and money."
He said Kaczynski had the legal right to choose a venue for the trial, and he chose California.
U.S. District Judge Dickinson Debevoise said he would make a ruling in a week. He said if he decides in favour of a New Jersey trial, it would follow the California trial.
"That would create too much confusion to have a trial here that may overlap with a trial in Sacramento," Debevoise said.

Kaczynski, 54, a former mathematics professor turned recluse, was arrested in April at his one-room cabin in rural Montana. Evidence recovered from the cabin included bomb parts, an original copy of the Unabomber's rambling anti-technology manifesto and a typewriter allegedly used to write it, FBI officials said.
The crowded Newark courtroom was quiet during the arraignment hearing, as spectators and members of the media stared intently at Kaczynski on the television screen.

The Justice Department said the case marked one of the first times a closed circuit teleconference has been used for a suspect's court appearance. The hi-tech remote system was designed to avoid the high cost and security problems of transporting Kaczynski across the country.
Keller entered a plea of not guilty on Kaczynski's behalf.
